chapters.headline: Dashboard model: 7.08% by Mar 2027 on baseline levers; 5 scenarios span 6.67–7.39%
chapters.dek: A structural dashboard model, not a forecast. Pick a scenario or move 21 levers — FX inflows, the budget, the SBV, credit, substitutes — and the rate, each group's contribution and the funding pressure recompute in the browser.
notes: The base path rises +1.18 pp by Mar 2027; +0.77 of it is funding pressure already built up by Sep 2026 (P = 7.50 against a neutral 4.24).Replayed in sample, the model already sat +0.35 pp above the posted rate in Sep 2026 (6.25% vs 5.9%): the Big-4 held rates under guidance; the projection inherits

Each bar is a group's cumulative contribution by the last month; the bars add up exactly to the total change.Money flows (FX, budget, SBV, credit) act through the funding-pressure index, so with a lag; markets & prices act directly.

The rate rises while P is above the neutral P* and falls while it is below; P adds up 12 months of funding gaps (credit outrunning new deposits).P* is the least certain number in the model: the two horizontal lines show two estimates.

A structural dashboard model, not a forecast or investment advice.Structural dashboard model, not a forecast. The base path assumes levers stay at same-month-last-year or latest values; the model tends to sit above Big-4 posted rates when the SBV guides banks to hold them. Not investment advice.

Fitted only on data to Mar-2025, the structural model predicts a rise from 4.6% to 5.521% by Sep-2026 (actual 5.9%): right direction, about 71% of the size, but about half a year late (Big-4 banks moved in Jan-Mar 2026; the model's pressure builds through mid-2026 and reaches 5.5% only in Sep-2026).
